note.text: Communication exchanges information between senders and receivers through a channel. In the wider geographical study, communication systems include transport and telecommunications: transport moves people or goods, while telecommunications transmits information over distance. Networks connect nodes through links. A line on a map shows a connection only within its legend; it does not prove a reliable or affordable service.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish information exchange from physical transport and identify network elements. Builds on: location and access. Leads to: road and rail development.

sections.heading: Explain the geography
sections.text: Communication exchanges information between senders and receivers through a channel. In the wider geographical study, communication systems include transport and telecommunications: transport moves people or goods, while telecommunications transmits information over distance. Networks connect nodes through links. A line on a map shows a connection only within its legend; it does not prove a reliable or affordable service.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: In a fictional Buea trading case, Bih phones a supplier to place an order and a carrier later brings the goods. The call exchanges information; the vehicle transports goods. The shop and depot are nodes, while a road is a transport link. A reply can confirm that the message was received and understood.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: State what moves, identify its channel and name the connected nodes. Distinguish a connection’s existence from its quality. Check whether a reply gives feedback or whether the message could have been misunderstood.
